tob-10450: The German mystic Jakob Boehme wrote these dialogues as a conversation between a master and his pupil about the nature of God and the soul. His dense, visionary prose explores how darkness gives birth to light and how the divine reveals itself in creation. Reading Boehme demands patience, but few thinkers have pushed further into the mystery of existence. This volume renders his work in English.
tob-4050: This volume of Wordsworth’s gathered works carries his verse into middle age — the sonnets, the longer musings, and the poems of travel and loss. The blaze of youth settles into the thoughtful voice that made him poet laureate. Readers can trace a great poet’s ripening across a long and crowded life.
tob-13450: Paramananda’s Englishing of the Upanishads opens the forest-lore of old India — the deep talks on the All-Soul, the Self, and the One behind all. These are the crown of Vedic thought, the well of Vedanta. His plain rendering made the mystic books speak to western seekers.
tob-0150: Aleister Crowley’s Magick in Theory and Practice is latter-day wonder-working’s bible — his Thelema rule, rite-craft, and teaching of the True Will. Half schoolbook, half spell-book, it binds his needful lore. The book has swayed every wonder-worker since.
tob-4150: Nicholson’s second Mathnawi book carries Rumi’s great godly epic onward — more tales and teachings in the famed rhymed pairs men call the Persian Koran. His rendering with gloss stays the English Rumi past gainsaying. The work deepens the West’s draught of Sufi song.
tob-9350: Philo’s Special Laws unfolds Moses’ law for the Greek-tongued world — the Alexandria Jew’s great gloss on Exodus and Leviticus. His hidden-sense way wed Jewry to Greek thought. Church fathers mined his hidden readings a thousand years. The work swayed Christian writ-reading for ages to come.
tob-13150: F. Max Muller’s Six Thought-Frames of India musters Nyaya, Vaiseshika, Samkhya, Yoga, Mimamsa, and Vedanta — the six right-believing schools. The great east-scholar’s talks made Hindu thought open to the western world. The book stays the classic English door to the darshanas.
cia-0000102950: An intelligence briefing from September 1984 on crime and the justice system in the Soviet Union. It lays out how the Soviets defined crimes, ran their courts, and punished offenders, giving American readers a clear picture of law and order behind the Iron Curtain. The report reflects Washington's steady interest in the everyday machinery of the Soviet state, not just its missiles.
cia-0000107450: An October 1948 report on meetings between representatives of Arab communist parties. Communists across the Middle East were coordinating as the region convulsed over Palestine and independence. The document shows American intelligence tracking an ideology's organization chart in a part of the world Washington was just beginning to understand.
cia-0000112350: A January 1991 report on a Moravian UFO later thought to be a falling satellite. Czechoslovakia's Moravia region watched a light cross the sky; experts offered the likeliest explanation — space junk burning up. The entry shows the mundane truth behind many sightings, preserved by an agency that checked them all.
cia-0000118650: An intelligence memorandum dated February 1968 — the archive gives no subject line. Memos without titles in the catalog keep their contents for the reader of the full text. The entry records only the form and date: the CIA writing to itself, as it did every day of the Vietnam War.
cia-0000119750: Hungary as of 10:00 PM on November 5, 1956 — the day after Soviet tanks rolled back into Budapest to crush the revolution. Resistance was collapsing into desperate street fighting. The document records the revolution's darkest hours, timestamp by timestamp.
cia-0000132650: A May 1960 report: Castro now prepared for the early seizure of Western refineries. The oil showdown was coming — Havana ready to take the plants. The document is the seizure, planned: the refineries, targeted.
cia-0000132750: A 1961 document titled Cuban, with the rest deleted by censors. The single surviving word promises a Cuba file; the redaction keeps the rest. The entry is the mystery: the subject, withheld.
cia-0000134250: A 1960 item: the West on Cuba, plus a late item on USSR-Cuba. The roundup with a bulletin. The document is the update: the West, the East, and the late news.
cia-0000136150: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on RENNELL. The cryptonym, referenced. The document is the name: the RENNELL, noted.
cia-0000136350: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN providing data on aircraft involved in PBSUCCESS — the truncated title cuts off the details. The air fleet, itemized. The document is the data: the planes, listed.
cia-0000139450: A 1988 file titled Project Sun Streak — the military's remote-viewing program, psychics spying by mind. The paranormal, funded. The document is the project: the viewing, remote.
un-ga-res-a-69-50: General Assembly Resolution A/69/50, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The fiftieth act. The designation and year align; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-250: Security Council Resolution 250, adopted in 1968. The Council's business continued. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-450: Security Council Resolution 450, adopted in 1979 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1350: Security Council Resolution 1350, adopted in 2001 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1650: Security Council Resolution 1650, adopted in 2006 — aligned. The new year's Council deciding. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1850: Security Council Resolution 1850, cataloged with the year 2009 — the historical record places this Annapolis peace-process resolution in December 2008, backing the Israeli-Palestinian negotiations. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
plos-pone-0000050: A 2006 PLOS ONE study: human natural killer T cells are heterogeneous in their capacity to respond — the truncated title cuts off to what. Immune cells, diverse in their reactions. The paper is the heterogeneity: the cells, varied.
gregory-great-morals-on-job-vol-3-part-1: Volume 3, Part 1 of Gregory's Morals on the Book of Job, translated in 1850 — the commentary's third volume begins. Gregory's moral reading of Job's suffering, sustained across hundreds of pages. The book is the persistence: the exegesis, immense.
gregory-great-morals-on-job-vol-3-part-2: Volume 3, Part 2 of the Morals on Job, covering Books XXX through XXXV, in the 1850 translation — the commentary's final stretch. Gregory's great work on suffering concludes. The volume is the conclusion: the morals, complete.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d50: The President to the Secretary of State, October 21, 1943 — Document 50. The same day, the answer. The message is the swiftness: the reply, same-day.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d150: The Joint Chiefs of Staff to the ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 150. The war's planners wrote Moscow's envoy. The memo is the planners': the chiefs, to Harriman.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d250: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 250. The quarter-millennium mark — the editors' note. The note is the milestone: the count, 250.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d350: The president's secretary Early to the president's special assistant — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 350. The staff wrote the insider. The memo is the staff's: Early, to the assistant.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d450: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 450. The editors' bridge. The note is the bridge: the narrative, carried over.
arxiv-2605-08750: Humans describe sounds effortlessly — rough, hollow, bright — but machines struggle to put audio into words. Emanuele Rossi and Emanuele Rodolà study how to bridge that gap, building systems that communicate sound through natural language. Their 2026 paper tackles both directions of the problem: turning raw audio into meaningful descriptions and grounding words back in sound.
arxiv-2605-08950: Knowing which words will trip up language learners powers better textbooks and reading apps. Wicaksono Leksono Muhamad, Joanito Agili Lopo, and colleagues improve lexical difficulty prediction with context-aligned contrastive learning and ridge ensembles. The 2026 paper is educational NLP: grading word difficulty more accurately.
arxiv-2605-08850: Constrained optimization often relies on a linear minimization oracle — a subroutine that solves the easy linear version. Peter Richtárik and Kaja Gruntkowska localize it: Local LMO performs constrained gradient optimization using only local oracle calls. The 2026 paper is optimization theory that keeps computation close to home.
arxiv-2605-09150: Nash equilibrium play never loses in poker, but it leaves money on the table against weak opponents. Vlad Murgoci, Matthijs Spaan, and Yaniv Oren go beyond equilibrium with AlphaExploitem, learning to exploit suboptimal players. The 2026 paper is game AI that preys on mistakes.
arxiv-2605-09250: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals — small objects spiraling into spinning black holes — broadcast gravitational waves that future detectors will hear. Changkai Chen, Zhoujian Cao, and Jiliang Jing compute the wave fluxes from generic Kerr orbits efficiently and stably, via a unified confluent-Heun framework. The 2026 paper is gravitational-wave astronomy infrastructure.
arxiv-2605-09650: Training an AI agent depends as much on the workspace — tools, data pipelines, scaffolding — as on the learning algorithm. Elad Sarafian, Gal Kaplun, Ron Banner, and colleagues optimize the workspace itself. The 2026 paper is a trainer's manual: how to train your agent well.
arxiv-2605-09950: Boruta selects features by comparing them against randomized shadow copies; GPU implementations handle high-dimensional data at real speed. Xurui Li, Zhiguo Gan, Jiaming Zhang, and colleagues build novel GPU Boruta algorithms. The 2026 paper is feature selection accelerated. It brings shadow-based selection to the GPU era.
plos-pone-0003450: Evolutionary geneticists caught bacteria swapping control wiring in this 2008 paper. Several genes of Streptococcus pyogenes, the strep-throat pathogen, looked borrowed from another species, replaced by foreign counterparts. The team tested how those swapped genes rewired the circuitry controlling pilus production, showing that stolen DNA can reprogram a pathogen's surface machinery.
plos-pone-0003550: Ocean modelers asked why viruses carry stolen solar panels in this 2008 paper. Marine viruses that infect photosynthetic bacteria often carry the psbA gene for a photosynthesis protein, and Bragg and Chisholm modeled how that loot pays off for the virus. The fitness math explains one of the ocean's strangest cases of genetic piracy.
plos-pone-0003650: In 2008, a team watched a cancer gene rewrite DNA's wrapping. The Myc protein, a master switch for cell growth, landed on its target genes and changed the marks on their histones, the spools DNA winds around. The pattern of marks shows how one gene can reset whole growth plans from the packing level.
plos-pone-0003750: In 2008, Sáenz, Azpitarte, and Armañanzas profiled gene activity in a muscle-wasting disease. Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy 2A, caused by calpain 3 mutations, got its first broad expression portrait. The profile shows which genes go awry when this muscle protein fails.
plos-pone-0003850: In 2008, a team tied a new gene to runaway insulin in newborns. Mutations in UCP2 were found in children with congenital hyperinsulinism, revealing the protein's role in regulating insulin release. The finding adds a fresh genetic cause to a dangerous condition of low blood sugar in infants.
plos-pone-0003950: In 2008, Brechot, Gomez, and Bignon found retuned immune cells saving starved limbs. Shifting macrophage activation states protected tissue from death during critical limb ischemia in mice. The immune retuning offers a new angle on saving limbs from blocked arteries.
plos-pone-0004050: In 2008, Okech, Mwobobia, and Kamau fought malaria with everything at once. Integrated malaria management combined several control interventions across rural Kenya's Mwea division. Malaria cases at the local hospital fell as the program rolled out. The success shows combined measures beating malaria better than solo efforts.
plos-pone-0004150: In 2009, a team found gene favoritism everywhere in human genomes. Allele-specific gene expression proved widespread across the genome and many life processes. One parent copy often outworked the other copy. The bias helps explain human trait shifts and disease risk.
plos-pone-0004250: In 2009, a team caught an antioxidant badly backfiring. Mito-targeted coenzyme Q raised harmful superoxide in vessel cells. The mitoQ compound shifted fuel choice too. The paradox warns that targeted antioxidants can misfire. The result urges caution in mitochondria drug design.
plos-pone-0004350: In 2009, Martuszewska, Ljungberg, and Johansson found a brake on wandering cell crawling. Tensin3 proved a negative regulator of cell migration indeed. All four tensin family members fell silent in many cancers. The brake's sad loss may free tumor cells to roam.
plos-pone-0358950: Getting teenagers moving in PE class is a constant battle for teachers. This study tested whether game-like touches — points, badges, leaderboards — could raise students’ motivation in physical education. The researchers measured how motivation shifted when these gamified elements were added, offering schools concrete ideas for making exercise feel less like a chore.
plos-pone-0358750: During labor, big decisions — from pain relief to emergency interventions — often have to be made fast. This study examines how those choices get made: who receives information, who gets involved, and whether mothers feel like partners in the process. Drawing on experiences in maternity care, it points to what helps women feel genuinely part of the decisions about their own births.
plos-pone-0358550: Caregivers know health systems’ flaws firsthand — but are rarely given a real voice. This photovoice protocol will build capacity in health systems with and for caregivers, using their own photographs as evidence. The method turns lived experience into fuel for reform, with caregivers as co-researchers rather than subjects.
plos-pone-0358250: Nurses are the front line against choking — but do they know enough about swallowing disorders? This paper developed and validated a dysphagia knowledge and self-reported competence questionnaire for nurses. The tool reveals training gaps clearly, before patients pay the price for them.
plos-pone-0357950: Not all BCG vaccine strains train the immune system equally. This paper compared BCG-Russia and BCG-TICE on trained immunity, with direct implications for bladder cancer immunotherapy. The strain differences it found could change which BCG formulation doctors choose for their patients.
plos-pone-0357050: Does physical activity during pregnancy predict healthier outcomes? This HUNT study compared device-measured physical activity among women with and without adverse pregnancy outcomes. The objective accelerometer data replace self-report guesswork with hard evidence about movement and maternal health.
plos-pone-0355550: Whole genome sequencing can catch hospital outbreaks early — if it’s affordable enough to run routinely. This paper described methods for cost-efficient whole genome sequencing surveillance for enhanced outbreak detection in hospitals. The streamlined methods bring genomic epidemiology within reach of ordinary hospitals.
plos-pone-0355650: Staging lymph nodes in lung cancer determines treatment — and CT radiomics can sharpen it. This paper correlated CT radiomics features with histopathology for mediastinal lymph node staging in non-small cell lung cancer. The imaging signatures help oncologists stage more accurately without extra biopsies.
plos-pone-0348450: H1N1 influenza pneumonia has stalked Vietnam since the 2009 pandemic. This 10-year cohort study tracked ICU admission and mortality in adult patients with H1N1-related pneumonia. The decade of data reveals how the virus’s threat evolved — and whether care kept pace.
plos-pone-0356250: Poor sleep and type 2 diabetes are linked — but not in a straight line. This cross-sectional study of community patients with chronic diseases found a nonlinear relationship between sleep quality and diabetes prevalence. The curve reveals that both too little and too much sleep carry metabolic costs.
plos-pone-0355850: Training AI to classify emphysema subtypes on CT scans needs more data than exists. This paper compared generative versus classical synthetic data augmentation for the task. The head-to-head evaluation shows which synthetic-data strategy genuinely improves diagnosis of this debilitating lung disease.
plos-pone-0355950: Microcystin-RR — a cyanobacterial toxin — may be broken down by microbes without oxygen. This paper inferred a putative anaerobic transformation pathway using nitrogen-15 labeling and multi-omics in enriched shrimp pond sediment communities. The elucidated pathway could inform bioremediation of toxin-contaminated aquaculture ponds.
plos-pone-0356550: Medical devices can cause pressure injuries — and nurses are the first line of defense. This cross-sectional study assessed nurses’ knowledge and attitudes toward device-related pressure injuries in intensive care and surgical units. The findings expose training gaps that, once closed, could spare patients painful and preventable harm.
plos-pone-0356650: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. It amends the paper on conventionally versus organically fertilized tomatoes maintaining fruit quality through uncontrolled green peach aphid infestation, with transcriptomic analysis. Readers should consult the corrected version for the accurate record.
plos-pone-0349850: Radioactive iodine treatment for thyroid cancer works better with the right patient selection. This paper examined how the stimulated thyroglobulin/TSH ratio and N1b lymph node status affect first I-131 treatment efficacy across differentiated thyroid cancer patients. The findings refine who benefits most from this targeted therapy.
plos-pone-0354450: Older adults with type 2 diabetes often face social isolation on top of chronic illness. This qualitative study explored their experiences of that isolation. The intimate accounts reveal how diabetes management and loneliness feed each other — and what kinds of connection genuinely help these patients thrive rather than merely survive.
plos-pone-0354150: China’s first imported mpox case ignited a Weibo firestorm — of fear, stigma, and information. This sentiment analysis study tracked real-time emotional dynamics and public discourse on Sina Weibo afterward. The findings reveal how a novel pathogen’s arrival moves a digital public — essential for crisis communication.
plos-pone-0331050: COVID-19 mortality risk rose and fell in complex, non-monotonic patterns. This paper built a flexible exponential-type family for modeling such hazard rates, applied to mortality analysis. The statistical family gives epidemiologists better tools for the next pandemic’s waves.
plos-pone-0353750: A decade of aging looks different in Brazil than in Europe — and the WHO’s ICOPE framework captures it. This paper compared cross-continental patterns of functional performance in older adults across the two regions. The comparison reveals how social conditions, healthcare systems, and culture shape what aging feels like — with lessons for healthy-aging policy on both continents.
plos-pone-0346350: Diabetes patients in northern Nigeria face dyslipidemia that goes untreated and uncontrolled. This multicenter cross-sectional study measured prevalence, treatment rates, and control. The findings expose a cardiovascular time bomb — lipid disorders hiding inside the diabetes epidemic.
europmc-pmc2791750: Dairy farmers breed cows using DNA-based predictions of genetic merit, and this 2009 paper tests how accurate those predictions are across multiple cattle breeds. The authors check whether genomic breeding values hold up when breeds are mixed rather than purebred. More reliable predictions mean faster genetic progress in milk production.
europmc-pmc2808350: Replacing damaged light-sensing cells could restore vision, and this 2010 paper moves that goal closer. The authors generate photoreceptors from human induced pluripotent stem cells, purify them, and transplant them into animal eyes. They show the lab-grown cells survive and integrate. The study was an early proof that stem-cell-derived photoreceptors can take hold.
europmc-pmc2811150: Malaria in pregnancy puts two lives at risk, but how many face it? This 2010 head-count blends census data with malaria charts to tally pregnancies at risk in 2007. The team gives per-country sums. The sums gave health chiefs firm ground for shielding moms-to-be.
europmc-pmc2838750: Some genes help males but harm females, creating an evolutionary tug-of-war. This 2010 paper hunts for these sexually antagonistic genes in Drosophila melanogaster. The authors identify candidates where the sexes' interests clash. The study illuminates a hidden conflict shaping the genome.
europmc-pmc2848550: Gene maps link spots to illness, but proof of cause wants more. This 2010 paper hunts would-be cause knobs by wedding gene-switch maps to illness gene hits. The authors demo the match. Their ploy nudged gene sleuths from linked zones to likely gears.
europmc-pmc2859250: The malaria parasite's blood-stage gene activity was murky until RNA-Seq arrived. This 2010 paper brings fresh insight into the Plasmodium falciparum blood-stage transcriptome with deep sequencing. The authors map which genes switch on in red cells. Their data became a go-to resource for malaria drug hunters.
europmc-pmc2876750: Drug-proof staph jumped from farm animals to people. This 2007 paper documents methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus of animal origin turning up in humans. The authors' Dutch data rang alarms across Europe. Their finding tied livestock antibiotic use to human risk.
europmc-pmc2885750: The lab workhorse Bacillus subtilis got its genome sequenced by a consortium, then refined for a decade. This 2009 paper presents the unified reference genome of strain 168, ten years on. The authors clean and complete the sequence. Their polished genome anchors countless microbiology studies.
europmc-pmc2906150: The cell rust of exercise may be a signal, not just damage. This 2010 review argues these charged bits tell muscles how to adapt and grow stronger. The authors recast free radicals as messengers. Their view changed how athletes think about antioxidant pills.
europmc-pmc2915950: Stroke research in rodents needs good yardsticks to mean anything. This 2010 paper reviews functional assessments in the rodent stroke model, from paw tests to maze runs. The authors guide researchers on measuring true recovery. Their review raised the bar for preclinical stroke work everywhere.
europmc-pmc3024950: Lab cell lines carry distinct receptor profiles. This 2011 paper maps drug-target receptors across four popular cell lines. The authors' atlas guides drug testers. Their work aids smart cell-line choice. Wrong line, wrong results, they warn. The atlas is free for drug hunters.
europmc-pmc3037350: Malaria parasites pick a lock to invade cells. This 2011 paper shows two parasite proteins, RON2 and AMA1, must clasp to punch into cells. The authors reveal the lock. Their work points to vaccines. Blocking the clasp stops the invasion. The clasp is now a vaccine bullseye.
europmc-pmc3063350: The brain's brake steers motor learning. This 2011 paper shows the GABA chemical tunes how humans learn movements. The authors reveal the brake's role. Their work informs rehab. Less brake means faster early learning. Too little brake risks shaky control. Brain-stimulation trials build on the finding.
europmc-pmc6532150: Many cancers survive chemotherapy by disabling apoptosis, the cell's built-in self-destruct program. Necroptosis - a different, more inflammatory form of programmed death - offers a detour around that blockade. This review explains how the necroptosis machinery works and how drugs that trigger it could kill apoptosis-resistant tumors, turning the cell's backup death switch into a therapy.
europmc-pmc6542350: Ecologists often need curves, not straight lines - and data grouped by site, species, or year. Hierarchical generalized additive models handle both at once. This gentle introduction, built around the R package mgcv, shows field researchers how to fit flexible, multi-level models to messy ecological data without drowning in math.
europmc-pmc6603150: Plants wield reactive oxygen species as both messengers and weapons: the same molecules that signal growth can scorch cells under stress. This review explains how plants make, sense, and detoxify ROS to steer development and survive drought, heat, and attack. Mastering this chemistry is key to tougher crops.
europmc-pmc6650350: Brain tumors defy nearly every treatment thrown at them - and this expert review explains why. The challenges run from the blood-brain barrier to the tumors' invasive roots and shape-shifting cells. Curing primary brain cancers, the authors argue, demands attacking their unique biology, not borrowing other cancers' playbooks.
europmc-pmc6710350: The retina - brain tissue that sees - has its own resident immune guards: microglia. This review examines how these cells patrol the eye's delicate layers and what happens when their surveillance turns destructive in retinal degeneration. Keeping retinal microglia balanced could save sight.
europmc-pmc6744450: Melanoma's inflammation was blamed on T cells - but B cells are the real arsonists. This study shows tumor-associated B cells sustain the inflammation that predicts checkpoint-blockade response in human melanoma. The overlooked B cell becomes both a biomarker and a target.
europmc-pmc6761150: Macrophages come in flavors - and the healing M2 kind needs precise tuning. This study shows the Stat6/Trim24 crosstalk fine-tunes M2 polarization: a chemical tag on Stat6 dials the response up or down. The molecular dimmer switch could be turned therapeutically.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-50: Congress's audit arm, GAO, wrote this 2007 report on the State Children's Health Insurance Program. It compares how states set up their plans, signed up kids, spent money, and ran ad drives — with a close look at states that covered grown-ups too. The findings show which state plans and sales pitches did the best job of reaching families who qualified.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-750: Student-loan lenders were running wild in 2007 — GAO's report says the Education Department finally turned up the watch. The findings detail the tightened oversight of lender and school games in the federal loan program. The report captures the moment Washington noticed the student-loan gold rush.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-650: The weather service's new toy needed better plans in 2007 — GAO's report says the operations prototype wanted more rigorous groundwork first. The findings press for discipline before deployment. The report's moral: forecast the project with the same care you forecast the storms.
gao-gaoreports-b-308150: Housing in Cairo for Central Command drew GAO's fiscal eye in this March 2007 ruling, which tests the spending against the money law. The call reads the appropriations against the arrangement. The ruling decides whether the overseas housing deal was legally sound.
gao-gaoreports-b-299150: ITT Electronic Systems quintupled its February 2007 protest — five case numbers, one radar fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles them all. The firm challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Five filings get one thorough answer. The radar fight got a full radar sweep.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-150: Public television's money maze got a GAO look in 2007, and the report examines the structure and funding of the system. The findings map the dollars. The report asks who should pay for the programming the market would not. The airwaves' orphan needed a patron.
openalex-w7206176250: Delayed pressure urticaria causes painful red welts after prolonged pressure on the skin, and living with it can weigh heavily on the mind. This narrative review connects the medical and the mental: how the condition affects quality of life, and how the nervous and immune systems interact in it. The authors gather scattered research on a little-known chronic hives subtype, arguing that treatment should address mood and daily living, not just the rash.
openalex-w7204955450: Including an autistic child in school takes a team, and the family-school relationship can make or break it. This article examines how parents and schools work together around children on the autism spectrum, and the barriers, some obvious, some nearly invisible, that get in the way. The authors focus on what helps development and what quietly blocks it. Practical and empathetic, it treats inclusion as a shared project.
openalex-w7204238750: Polycystic ovary syndrome affects millions of women, and lifestyle pulls many of its strings. This paper reviews how diet, activity, and habits shape the metabolic and reproductive effects of PCOS. The authors link insulin resistance and weight to the condition. A women's-health review where daily choices meet hormones.
pmc-13470650: A 2026 cell biology paper on FLOWER (FWE), a protein that regulates how cells move material through endo-lysosome-related organelles — tiny cellular sorting stations. The authors show this one regulator works across many contexts, influencing how cells recycle and ship their contents. Understanding FWE could matter for diseases tied to broken cell transport.
pmc-13463750: A 2026 stroke study drawing on Norway's national stroke registry to compare outcomes of clot-busting treatment (thrombolysis) in patients with mild ischemic stroke. Using real-world registry data, it evaluates whether the treatment helps this debated group. The findings give clinicians evidence-based guidance for a common bedside dilemma.
pmc-13459750: A 2026 genomics paper on how yaks adapted to high altitudes, scanning the genome for links to blood and body traits. Living on the Tibetan plateau demands special physiology, and the study found polygenic adaptation — many small genetic changes working together. The work is a window into how mammals conquer extreme environments.
pmc-13493050: A 2026 computational chemistry paper on predicting how tightly drug candidates bind their protein targets without requiring the 3D structure up front. Using hierarchical representation alignment, the model learns from data across scales. Structure-agnostic prediction could widen early drug screening to targets whose shapes are still unknown.
pmc-13443050: This 2026 pathology paper found that GPNMB, a cell-surface protein, is strongly expressed in foreign body giant cells — the fused immune cells that form around implants and debris — in both human and mouse tissues. A shared marker across species strengthens its value for studying implant reactions. The finding could help monitor how bodies respond to medical devices.
pmc-13485350: In this 2026 rheumatology paper, high levels of VCAM-1 — vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 — marked a "vasculopathic" phenotype in systemic sclerosis patients with higher mortality. Blood vessel damage drives much of scleroderma's danger, and VCAM-1 flags the worst-affected. The biomarker could sharpen prognosis.
pmc-13459550: In this 2026 bioinformatics paper, the authors built MSstatsQC-ML, a supervised machine learning approach to monitor system suitability and quality control in mass spectrometry-based proteomics. Instruments drift; catching it early saves experiments. The ML monitor automates what technicians now eyeball.
pmc-13449250: A 2026 phylogenetics paper drawing on over 50 newly sequenced organellar genomes to illuminate the phylogeny and enigmatic mitochondrial biology of eustigmatophyte algae. These algae have bizarre mitochondria. The genome haul resolves relationships and deepens the mystery.
pmc-13323950: This 2026 review surveys emerging immune-based therapeutic strategies in hepatocellular carcinoma — liver cancer. Immunotherapy has been slower to crack liver cancer than other tumors. The review maps the strategies trying to change that.
pmc-13369950: This 2026 cohort study examined blood pressure and cardiovascular risk in young adults. Risk starts accumulating early. The contemporary data update the picture for a new generation.
pmc-13591650: A 2026 bioengineering paper on ultrathin hydrogel membranes inspired by soap films enabling physiologically relevant breathing lung models. The lung-on-chip breathed realistically. The membrane is the innovation.
pmc-13448350: A 2026 conference abstract (CLTR-01) on surgical selection patterns in NSCLC brain metastases — clinical and molecular correlates in the TKI era. Targeted therapies changed the surgical calculus. The abstract maps the patterns.
pmc-13487450: This 2026 review covered multi-omics-guided design and safety engineering of nucleic acid therapeutics — from molecular perturbation to predictive toxicology (the title is truncated). The omics-guided safety is the paradigm. The review maps it.
pmc-13478750: In this 2026 bioinformatics paper, Binary-SPA — a reference-free method for cell annotation in high-resolution spatial transcriptomics — was introduced. The annotation without references is the advance. The method serves the field.
pmc-13470350: A 2026 comparative outcome analysis of leukocyte-rich versus leukocyte-poor platelet-rich plasma, injectable platelet-rich fibrin, and corticosteroids (the title is truncated). The orthobiologics were head-to-head. The comparison guides injections.
pmc-13468750: A 2026 pilot study on step count as a digital mobility outcome — differences between upper and lower extremities. The wrist versus ankle counts were compared. The pilot explores the metric.
pmc-13454950: A 2026 case report of myocardial infarction complicated with blood pressure fluctuations caused by pheochromocytoma. The adrenal tumor's catecholamine storms explained the swings. The case is the lesson.
pmc-13456850: In this 2026 MIMIC-IV analysis, the blood glucose-to-platelet ratio was associated with all-cause mortality in diabetic patients. The simple ratio predicted death. The association is the risk tool.
